raw_response:
*In the voice of the farmer:*

Ai, four mu and a little, that's all I've got. But me and my old woman, plus the kids when they come back from the factory, we manage it fine. I've been working this dirt since I was a boy. Fifty-five years — my hands know what to do before my head does.

Here's how I'm thinking about this year. The cotton is my main thing, like most folks on our side of the village. I put about 2 mu to cotton. On another piece I do wheat in winter and maize after — that's 1 mu of ground, two crops on the same patch, that's how we always did it. The last bit, about a mu and a little, I do stevia. The company in the county buys it, pays okay if the leaves are good. My nephew started doing it a few years back, said it wasn't too hard for an old man, so I tried it and stuck with it.

**Cotton** — I'll plant around Guyu (谷雨), middle of April, when the ground warms up. Same Bt seed the agent in town sells, everybody uses it now because of the bollworm. About half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu before I plow, then when the cotton starts squaring I side-dress some urea. Maybe 12-13 kg of nitrogen per mu all told — I don't measure exact, I go by the bag. I'll water it twice from the well if the sky doesn't help, but the electricity for pumping is not cheap, so I wait until the leaves start to droop. Spraying for bugs is a must, otherwise you get nothing. Picking is what kills my back — I get my daughter-in-law and the grandkids when they're off school.

**Wheat** — Goes in around mid-October after I clear the maize. I use saved seed from last year, it does fine on our land. Put down a bag of compound before sowing, then topdress urea in spring when it greens up. Water three times if the rain is short — returning green, jointing, and when the grain is filling. If I skip the filling water the grain is shriveled, I learned that long ago. Herbicide once in spring for the grass. I usually get around 400 kg a mu, some years 450 if the spring rains are good.

**Maize** — Goes in right after the wheat combine leaves, no time to plow, I just drill it straight in. Hybrid seed from the shop — can't save hybrid seed, everyone knows that. Fertilizer goes down with the seeder, then I put more urea at the big trumpet stage when the plant is tall. One watering usually, two if July is dry. Spray herbicide early. Hope for 450 kg a mu.

**Stevia** — Seedlings are expensive, that's the hard part. I buy them from the company, plant them in April when it's warm enough. They like a bit of manure — I still have the yard chickens and a pig, so I spread what I have, plus some compound fertilizer. Water two or three times. Don't spray much, the company doesn't like chemicals on it. Cut the leaves when the plant is ready, dry them on the roof. Main cost is the seedlings and the labor to cut, but mostly I do it myself.

Money is always tight with four mu. I can't put fertilizer like a business farm does. I just do what my neighbors do, more or less, and what worked last year.
